prior_coverage: Most of this family was swept before, and I reopened nothing without new evidence. (1) The israel-bureaucracy group (8 scouts, 3.9) left two standing walls: the Tax Authority is a gate, not a platform, and the state is our free competitor (docs/REJECTED.md:156-211). The group's audited ceiling is ₪500-1,500/month across all lines (audits/israel-bureaucracy.md). (2) The israeli-smb-software scout covered Morning, iCount, Rivhit and Hashavshevet (scouts/israel-bureaucracy--israeli-smb-software.md). Morning's 'חבר מביא חבר' pays account credit, not money (groups/israel-bureaucracy.md:220). The iCount partner programme was confirmed at up to 15% for 3 years, paid by bank transfer once ₪100 accrues, against a receipt per payout; the audit cut it to ₪0-100/month (groups/israel-bureaucracy.md:43,171-185; audits/israel-bureaucracy.md:420-460). Reselling Rivhit's modules needs a human sales relationship (groups:221). A paid Israeli-bureaucracy ebook was killed because skills-il gives the same content away free (groups:218). Municipal SaaS was killed because the buyer is an authority buying through tenders (groups:215). (3) distribution--israeli-channels: Facebook groups, WhatsApp and Israeli forums are closed to an automated poster. (4) tenders-occupancy.md: 17 sellers plus free state sources, so this is not a venue for us. eaa-occupancy.md: closed. (5) The Israeli B2B app stores were covered by the sibling breadth scout research/breadth/scouts/app-plugin-marketplaces.json. There, Wix App Market is PROMISING at rank 1 with Israel payout UNKNOWN, and monday.com is DEAD because Payoneer needs a face scan for Israeli residents. I list Wix below only as a cross-reference for its Hebrew angle, which was never taken (REJECTED.md:966-968); count it once. NEW this sweep, with grades: (a) e-vrit (עברית), which describes itself as Israel's largest Hebrew digital book store, carries independent authors under a 'הוצאה עצמית' publisher page, Publisher/746 (snippet). It also exposes a public JSON product API: third-party code pages through /api/group/286/products and reports about 27,108 titles in its public-library group alone (github: revrevrev/Libraries-search CLAUDE.md). A GitHub runner can therefore count self-published titles and their ratings for free. The only e-vrit APIs in public code are reader, search and download endpoints; no publisher-upload API was seen (github). (b) Indiebook has an 'e-הוצאה עצמית' category and a 'royalty report guide for independent authors' page (snippet), which implies a self-serve author back office. Its only scale figure (350 books, 2013) is stale. (c) Morning's API has a 4-endpoint Partners group: 'Get all connected users', 'Request user approval' and two more (github: danielrosehill/GreenInvoice-MCP API_REFERENCE.md). That is integrator access to a user's own account, not a store. Its add-ons page lists integrations (snippet), and no third-party paid marketplace was found. (d) No paid Israeli teacher-to-teacher marketplace surfaced. The Hebrew results were free lesson-plan sites such as kanlomdim, achiyayeda and hanoch.info (snippet). (e) Google Play Books: a snippet says Israel is not on the 70%-split country list, and that payouts need a local business address and bank account in a supported payment country. (f) Facebook Marketplace bans digital products (snippet). Structural finding for the family: Israeli venues pay by Israeli bank transfer against a tax receipt per payout. That mostly solves the payout rail but ties every line to owner step 2 (osek patur) plus an automated receipt path. None of them offers a documented listing API. The Hebrew moat is real only where a big Hebrew buyer pool exists (e-vrit, Wix's Hebrew SMB base). Not reached for lack of budget: SUMIT, Priority and Hashavshevet partner marketplaces, the Education Ministry's Gefen programme catalogue, TpT's Hebrew section, and Hebrew font marketplaces.
